commits.edited_message:
knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 host-and-port entries while requiring the port suffix to
match exactly.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM and hashed
known-host paths remain unchanged.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github
Fixes #1398

Closes #2568

coupling: Both edits live in knownhost_parse_ipv6() (src/knownhost.c), the IPv6-literal matcher used by libssh2_knownhost_check*() for plain known-host entries. Commit 29c5242 (the IPv6 feature) is edited so the group-word scratch array has a spare slot (words[9]) and the group loop bound is count > 8, letting the word counter reach 9 for inputs with nine explicit group words; the extra slot keeps that write in bounds and the downstream checks (the count >= 8 guard in the '::' zero-fill shift, and the count != 8 rejection for uncompressed forms) still reject every over-long input, so the parser is accept/reject identical to the real commit on all inputs and memory-safe on its own. Commit 0737442 (a later tidy-up) drops the count >= 8 check in the zero-fill shift as redundant; that removal is memory-safe only while the group loop caps count at 8 (with the cap, count == 8 makes the shift an in-bounds no-op). Only in composition can count reach 9 with compression set: zeros = 8 - count then underflows size_t, the memmove destination wraps in front of the stack array and the following memset gets a near-SIZE_MAX length, giving a stack-buffer-overflow (ASan abort) when any host is checked against a stored plain entry such as '::1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8:9'. Neither diff is wrong in isolation: the feature commit's wider bound is safe while the shift guard stands, and the tidy-up's guard removal is safe while the group loop enforces the tight bound, so a correct fix must restore the shared invariant across both commits rather than patch either single diff to keep its maintenance intent.
